title: PySpark: when does this chain run?

children.text: Given a filter and groupBy chain, explain lazy evaluation and identify what triggers execution.

items: Explain the output grain after groupBy.
Expect aggregation to require data redistribution in typical cases.
Use an execution plan to discuss the actual physical stages.

children.text: The transformations describe a computation. An action such as show asks Spark to produce a result. Multiple actions can repeat work unless appropriate results are persisted; caching is a resource decision, not a universal speed fix.

children.code:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

# Assumes orders is a Spark DataFrame with customer_id, status, net_amount.
paid = orders.filter(F.col('status') == 'PAID')
totals = paid.groupBy('customer_id').agg(
    F.sum('net_amount').alias('revenue')
)
totals.show()  # An action requests results.

children.title: Watch for this
children.text: The assignment to totals is not an action. Calling show twice should not be assumed to reuse the first computed result.

items: Where might you persist data when two downstream consumers use the same expensive transformation?
